subsystems.name: Matrix compute array
subsystems.role: the arithmetic engine; multiplies and accumulates weight and activation matrices.

subsystems.name: On-chip memory and buffering
subsystems.role: keeps weights and activations close to the arithmetic so the array is not starved.

subsystems.name: System memory interface
subsystems.role: large language models are too big for on-chip SRAM, so weights stream from shared low-power DRAM.
parts: unified memory shared with CPU and GPU

subsystems.name: Quantisation and compiler stack
subsystems.role: shrinks a trained model to 4- or 8-bit weights and maps it onto the hardware.

subsystems.name: Heterogeneous SoC fabric
subsystems.role: lets the NPU hand work to CPU, GPU or DSP when a layer suits them better.

subsystems.name: Runtime and OS integration
subsystems.role: apps call the accelerator through a stable driver rather than touching registers.

buildSteps.title: Profile target models
buildSteps.detail: Engineers measure the layer shapes, precision and memory traffic of the transformer models the chip must run, which sets array size and buffer depths.

buildSteps.title: Write and verify the RTL
buildSteps.detail: The design is described in a hardware description language and checked in simulation against a software reference model, including quantisation rounding.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise and place-and-route
buildSteps.detail: The logic is mapped to standard cells and a target foundry node, then timing, power and area are closed.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the die
buildSteps.detail: Photomasks are made and wafers are processed at a leading-edge node — the transistor density is what makes room for a large accelerator alongside CPU and GPU.

buildSteps.title: Test and bin
buildSteps.detail: Dies are probed, defective blocks are disabled, and parts are sorted by the clock speed they can hold at a given voltage.

buildSteps.title: Package with memory
buildSteps.detail: The SoC die is assembled with stacked low-power DRAM in one package, or as chiplets on a silicon interposer.

buildSteps.title: Bring up firmware
buildSteps.detail: Boot code, clocking, thermal limits and power states are tuned on real silicon.

buildSteps.title: Ship kernels and tooling
buildSteps.detail: Operators are hand-optimised, model conversion tools are released, and frameworks add backends so developers can target the accelerator.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into devices
buildSteps.detail: Phone, laptop and embedded operating systems expose the NPU through their inference APIs and decide when to use it.

prerequisites.why: a dedicated accelerator only pays off when hundreds of millions of transistors fit in a small power budget.
generate one token requires reading essentially every weight, so memory bandwidth — not compute — is the usual limit.
4-bit and 8-bit weights cut model size several-fold with modest quality loss, making local execution practical.
optimised kernels, key-value caching and scheduling are needed to get usable token rates.
mapping arbitrary new model architectures onto fixed-function arrays still often requires manual work.

pathway.milestone: tens of TOPS NPUs in phones and laptops running few-billion-parameter quantised models
pathway.unlocks: private, offline assistants, live transcription and on-device image generation at a few tokens per second.

pathway.milestone: unified memory pools of tens of gigabytes at hundreds of gigabytes per second
pathway.unlocks: locally running larger models without cloud round-trips.

pathway.milestone: hardware support for mixture-of-experts routing, sparsity and speculative decoding
pathway.unlocks: far higher effective speed because only part of the model is read per token.
breaking the bandwidth wall, since weights are read where they are stored.

pathway.milestone: co-designed chips for specific model families
pathway.unlocks: efficiency that general-purpose NPUs cannot match, at the cost of flexibility.
